text:
Mathieu Joseph is on his fifth NHL team and his first season in Edmonton, a two-time Cup winner from Tampa doing fourth-line work for the Oilers. The scoring line looks fine for that role: 4 goals and 11 points in 27 games, already matching his 51-game total in St. Louis last season, including a shorthanded goal at Carolina on Nov. 21.

The five-on-five picture is the worry. Edmonton takes only 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 12 points worse than without him, and his 18.2% shooting sits well above his range. Some of those points are on borrowed time.

That said, his case was never offense. Evolving-Hockey rated his 2025-26 value mostly from even-strength defense and credited him with drawing more penalties than he takes, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found 75% of his shots came off the rush. His minutes jumped to 16.5 and 15.4 in the last two games; watch whether the chances against follow him up the lineup.
headline: Joseph's points are ahead of his process
